docs.title: Jira Transition Runner
docs.text: A Python CLI tool (with optional GUI) for bulk Jira issue transitions with hierarchical support and smart planning.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Two-Phase Workflow

  • Phase 1 (Plan) — Generate an Excel plan with dropdown validations and smart target-status defaults
  • Phase 2 (Execute) — Execute approved transitions with parallel processing and retry logic

Version Management

  • Release and archive Jira fix versions in bulk
  • Validation before release (checks for unresolved issues)
  • Supports CLI input or Excel file; dry-run mode available

Hierarchical Issue Processing

  • Automatically discover child issues (subtasks, stories, epics, initiatives)
  • Filter by status category (exclude "Done" items)
  • Track open bugs across hierarchy levels
  • Auto-reject approval when open bugs exist

Smart Target Defaults

  • Auto-populate target_status with the highest-priority reachable status
  • Configurable priority order (e.g., Closed > Done > Cancelled)
  • BFS pathfinding for multi-step transitions
  • Visual indicators (blue bold) in the plan Excel; user can override via dropdown

Reliability

  • Rate-limit handling (respects Retry-After) and exponential backoff
  • Configurable concurrency and retry limits
  • Real-time Rich progress bars

Desktop GUI

  • Full tkinter GUI mirroring all CLI features — no terminal required

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# 1. Install
git clone <repository-url>
cd jira-transition-runner
uv sync

# 2. Configure — edit settings.toml (Jira URL, KeePass paths)
cp .env.example .env   # picks the environment: JIRA_ENV=development|staging|production

# 3. Phase 1: generate a plan
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml \
  --jql "project = PROJ AND status != Done" \
  --plan plan.xlsx --include-children

# 4. Review plan.xlsx, set approved=True for safe rows

# 5. Phase 2: dry-run first, then execute
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml --execute plan.xlsx --dry-run
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml --execute plan.xlsx

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.13+
  • uv (recommended) or pip
  • A KeePass database holding your Jira credentials

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url>
cd jira-transition-runner
uv sync

This installs all runtime dependencies declared in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Settings (settings.toml)
docs.text:
Settings are loaded with Dynaconf from settings.toml in the project root. The file has a [default] section plus one section per environment: [development], [staging] and [production]. An environment section only needs the keys that differ from [default].

[default]
# ── Required ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JIRA_BASE_URL = "https://your-domain.atlassian.net"

# KeePass database that stores the Jira credentials
KEEPASS_DB = "C:/keepass/Database.kdbx"
KEEPASS_KEY = "C:/keepass/Database.key"
KEEPASS_ENTRY = "Jira Entry Name"

# ── Concurrency ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JIRA_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 10   # simultaneous API requests
PHASE2_WORKERS = 15         # concurrent issue transitions in Phase 2

# ── Retry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JIRA_MAX_RETRIES = 3
JIRA_RETRY_BACKOFF_MIN = 2.0    # seconds
JIRA_RETRY_BACKOFF_MAX = 30.0   # seconds

# ── Rate limiting (HTTP 429) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
JIRA_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETRIES = 10   # retries per request for HTTP 429
JIRA_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT = 300     # seconds; fail if Jira asks to wait longer

# ── Status classification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DONE_STATUSES = ["Done", "Cancelled", "Closed"]
BUG_ISSUE_TYPES = ["Bug", "UAT Defect", "Production Defect"]   # case-insensitive
PRIORITY_STATUSES = ["Closed", "Done", "Cancelled"]            # smart-default order

# ── Mandatory field (Phase 2) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Set before transitioning these issue types if empty. Skipped in --dry-run.
# Use MANDATORY_FIELD_ID = "" to disable.
MANDATORY_FIELD_ID = "customfield_10000"
MANDATORY_FIELD_VALUE = "Some value"
MANDATORY_FIELD_ISSUE_TYPES = ["Bug", "UAT Defect"]

[development]
JIRA_BASE_URL = "https://your-sandbox.atlassian.net"
PHASE2_WORKERS = 2

[staging]
JIRA_BASE_URL = "https://your-sandbox.atlassian.net"

[production]
KEEPASS_ENTRY = "Jira (prod)"

docs.title: Choosing the environment
docs.text:
The active environment comes from JIRA_ENV and defaults to development. Set it in a .env file in the project root (see .env.example) or in the shell:

# .env
JIRA_ENV=production

$env:JIRA_ENV = "staging"; jira-runner ...

The CLI logs the active environment and Jira URL at startup, and the GUI shows them under Global settings.

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Highest precedence wins:

  1. settings.toml, the [default] section, then the active environment's section
  2. .secrets.toml (optional, git-ignored, same layout), for values you don't want committed
  3. JTR_-prefixed environment variables, including those in .env, e.g. JTR_PHASE2_WORKERS=5 or JTR_DONE_STATUSES='["Done", "Closed"]'

settings.toml is read from the current directory if it has one, otherwise from the project root. Set JTR_SETTINGS_DIR to use another directory.

docs.title: Workflow Configuration (transition.yaml)
docs.text:
Define per-project workflows. Each project maps issue types to workflows, and each workflow lists named transitions with from, to, and Jira transition id.

projects:
  PROJ:
    projectId: '10000'
    workflowSchemeId: 10001
    issueTypes:
      Story:
        workflow: Story_Workflow
        transitions:
          open_to_in_progress:
            id: '11'
            name: Start Progress
            from: Open
            to: In Progress
          in_progress_to_done:
            id: '21'
            name: Done
            from: In Progress
            to: Done

Tip

You can find transition IDs in Jira by navigating to Project Settings → Workflows and inspecting the transition links, or by calling GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions.

docs.title: Logging Configuration (logging_config.yaml)
docs.text:
The default config logs WARNING+ to the console and DEBUG+ to rotating files:

formatters:
  simple:
    format: '%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'

handlers:
  console:
    class: logging.StreamHandler
    level: WARNING
    formatter: simple
  file:
    class: logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler
    level: DEBUG
    filename: jira_transition_runner.log
    maxBytes: 10485760   # 10 MB
    backupCount: 5
    formatter: simple

Pass a custom config at runtime:

jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml --log-config my_logging.yaml ...

docs.title: "No path from X to Y"
docs.text:
The workflow graph has no transition path between the two statuses. Check transition.yaml:

  • Ensure all intermediate steps are defined (e.g., Open → In Progress → Done, not just Open → Done if the workflow requires it).
  • Verify the from/to status names match exactly what Jira uses (case-sensitive).

docs.title: Rate Limiting / Slow Execution
docs.text:
When Jira returns HTTP 429 (or 503 with Retry-After), the tool waits as long as Jira asks, pausing all requests together, and then retries. Rate-limited requests get their own retry budget, so a transition is never lost to a 429 unless the limit persists.

If the log shows frequent rate limits, or rows fail with Jira rate limit exceeded, reduce concurrency and allow more patience in settings.toml (in [default] or the active environment's section):

JIRA_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 5
PHASE2_WORKERS = 5
JIRA_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETRIES = 20
JIRA_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT = 600     # seconds

Rows that failed can be retried by running Phase 2 again on the same file; rows already in their target status are skipped.

docs.title: Authentication Failures
docs.text:
Authentication failed: ...

Check your KeePass config:

  • KEEPASS_DB path exists and is readable.
  • KEEPASS_KEY points to the correct key file.
  • KEEPASS_ENTRY matches the entry name exactly (case-sensitive).

docs.title: No Issues Found
docs.text:
⚠️  No issues found matching JQL
  • Test your JQL directly in Jira's issue navigator.
  • Ensure the authenticated user has permission to view those issues.

docs.title: Excel Dropdown Not Working
docs.text:
If target_status dropdowns are missing after opening the plan:

  • Open the file in Excel (not a third-party spreadsheet app).
  • Enable editing if prompted by the Protected View banner.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Enable detailed logging to diagnose unexpected behaviour:

# Watch the log file in real time
tail -f jira_transition_runner.log

Or pass a custom logging config:

jira-runner --log-config debug_logging.yaml --project PROJ ...

Where debug_logging.yaml sets the console handler level to DEBUG.

docs.title: Missing Transitions in Results
docs.text:
If a row shows FAILED with no transition found:

  1. Check the workflow_name column — ensure that workflow is defined in transition.yaml.
  2. Verify the issue's current status in Jira matches what the plan recorded (it may have changed since Phase 1).
  3. Confirm the Jira transition ID is correct for your Jira instance.

docs.title: GUI — Desktop Interface
docs.text: A tkinter-based GUI ships alongside the CLI and mirrors the full feature set — no terminal required.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
# Via installed script
jira-runner-gui

# Or directly
python -m jira_transition_runner.gui

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
The window has three sections:

  1. Global settings (top panel) — project key and workflow YAML path, shared by all tabs.
  2. Tab panel — one tab per operation mode.
  3. Output console (bottom) — live stdout/stderr stream with colour-coded tags.

docs.title: Global Settings
docs.text: Field Description Project key Jira project key (e.g. PROJ) Workflow YAML Path to transition.yaml; use Browse… to pick a file

docs.title: Phase 1 — Plan Tab
docs.text: Field Description JQL query Multi-line text area for your JQL Output Excel Destination file; defaults to plan.xlsx Include child issues Enables hierarchical lookup Generate Plan Runs Phase 1 in a background thread

docs.title: Phase 2 — Execute Tab
docs.text: Field Description Plan Excel file Plan file from Phase 1; use Browse… Dry run Simulates transitions without applying them Execute Plan Runs Phase 2 in a background thread

docs.title: Version Management Tab
docs.text: Field Description Action Release or Archive Versions source Manual (comma-separated) or From Excel file Version names / Excel file Input for version names Release date Defaults to today; edit for a custom date Dry run Simulates without applying changes Manage Versions Runs version management in a background thread

docs.title: Output Console
docs.text:
• Output is streamed in real time from the background thread.
  • ANSI escape sequences are stripped automatically.
  • Colour coding: normal output (grey), success (teal), warnings (yellow), errors (red).
  • Clear wipes the console; Copy all copies the full text to the clipboard.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• All operations run in a daemon thread — the UI stays responsive.
  • Only one operation can run at a time; all buttons are disabled while busy.
  • Settings (settings.toml and the JIRA_ENV environment) are loaded at startup the same way as the CLI. The active environment and Jira URL are shown under Global settings.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Generate Plan
docs.text: Phase 1 fetches Jira issues matching a JQL query, optionally enriches them with child issues, then writes an Excel plan file for human review.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
jira-runner \
  --project <KEY> \
  --yaml transition.yaml \
  --jql "<JQL>" \
  --plan <output.xlsx> \
  [--include-children]
Flag Required Description --project Yes Jira project key (e.g. PROJ) --yaml Yes Path to workflow YAML --jql Yes JQL to select issues --plan Yes Output Excel file path --include-children No Recursively fetch child issues

docs.title: With Hierarchy Lookup
docs.text:
jira-runner \
  --project PROJ \
  --yaml transition.yaml \
  --jql "project = PROJ AND issuetype = Epic AND status = 'QA Sign-off'" \
  --plan plan.xlsx \
  --include-children

Hierarchy levels resolved:

Level Type 2 Initiative 1 Epic 0 Story / Task -1 Subtask

Children with status category Done are excluded. If any child is an open bug (see BUG_ISSUE_TYPES in settings.toml), the parent row's approved column defaults to False and the bug keys appear in remarks.

docs.title: Without Hierarchy Lookup
docs.text:
jira-runner \
  --project PROJ \
  --yaml transition.yaml \
  --jql "project = PROJ AND sprint = 'Sprint 42'" \
  --plan plan.xlsx

Faster — skips child resolution. Useful when you only need to transition the queried issues themselves.

docs.title: Output Excel Format
docs.text:
Column Description issue_key Jira issue key summary Issue summary issuetype Issue type name current_status Status at time of plan generation target_status User selects — dropdown of valid target statuses; smart default pre-filled in blue bold approved User sets — True / False; auto-False when open bugs detected remarks Open bug keys, parent references

Smart Defaults

The target_status cell is pre-filled with the highest-priority reachable status (configured via PRIORITY_STATUSES). Override by selecting a different option from the dropdown before executing.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Execute Plan
docs.text: Phase 2 reads an approved plan Excel file and applies Jira transitions concurrently. Multi-step paths (e.g., Open → In Progress → Done) are resolved automatically via BFS on the workflow graph.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
jira-runner \
  --project <KEY> \
  --yaml transition.yaml \
  --execute <plan.xlsx> \
  [--dry-run]
Flag Required Description --project Yes Jira project key --yaml Yes Path to workflow YAML --execute Yes Plan Excel file (Phase 1 output) --dry-run No Simulate without applying changes

docs.title: Recommended Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Dry-run first to catch path errors
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml --execute plan.xlsx --dry-run

# 2. Execute live
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml --execute plan.xlsx

docs.title: What Gets Executed
docs.text: Only rows where approved is True, yes or 1 are processed. Other rows get status NOT_APPROVED. Rows already in their target status get SKIPPED.

docs.title: Dry Run
docs.text: --dry-run makes no changes in Jira. For each approved row it reads the current status, works out the route from the workflow YAML, and checks that Jira offers the first step. The execution_message column then shows the route, e.g. [DRY RUN] Would transition: Open → In Progress → Done. Later steps can only be checked against the YAML, because the issue doesn't actually move.

docs.title: Output Excel (*_results.xlsx)
docs.text:
The results file is written next to the input file with a _results suffix. It contains all input columns plus:

Column Description workflow_name Workflow used for the transition execution_status SUCCESS / FAILED / SKIPPED / NOT_APPROVED execution_message Error details when FAILED final_status Actual Jira status after execution executed_at ISO 8601 timestamp

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: Transitions run in parallel up to PHASE2_WORKERS (default 5, set in settings.toml). Rate-limited requests (HTTP 429) wait for Jira's Retry-After and are retried up to JIRA_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETRIES times. Network errors are retried up to JIRA_MAX_RETRIES times, but a transition is only re-sent if it never reached Jira. Other API errors fail the row immediately.

docs.title: Version Management
docs.text: Release or archive Jira fix versions in bulk, with automatic validation and dry-run support.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
jira-runner \
  --project <KEY> \
  --yaml transition.yaml \
  --manage-versions \
  --action <release|archive> \
  (--versions "Name 1, Name 2" | --versions-file versions.xlsx) \
  [--release-date YYYY-MM-DD] \
  [--dry-run]
Flag Required Description --manage-versions Yes Enable version management mode --action Yes release or archive --versions One of Comma-separated version names --versions-file One of Excel file with a version_name column --release-date No Release date in YYYY-MM-DD format; defaults to today --dry-run No Simulate without applying changes

docs.title: Release Versions
docs.text:
# From CLI
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml \
  --manage-versions --versions "Sprint 1.0, Sprint 2.0" --action release

# With a custom release date
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml \
  --manage-versions --versions "Q4 Release" --action release --release-date 2024-12-31

# From Excel
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml \
  --manage-versions --versions-file versions.xlsx --action release

docs.title: Archive Versions
docs.text:
jira-runner --project PROJ --yaml transition.yaml \
  --manage-versions --versions "Old Sprint 1, Old Sprint 2" --action archive

docs.title: Excel Input Format
docs.text:
The --versions-file Excel must have a single column named version_name:

version_name Sprint 1.0 Sprint 2.0 Q4 Release

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text: Condition Result Unresolved issues exist (release only) SKIPPED Version already released SKIPPED Version already archived SKIPPED Version not found in project FAILED Operation succeeded SUCCESS

docs.title: Output Report
docs.text:
Results are written to an Excel file:

  • From --versions-file input.xlsx → input_results.xlsx
  • From --versions "..." → {PROJECT}_{action}_versions_results.xlsx
Column Description version_name Version name version_id Jira version ID project_key Project key action_requested release or archive execution_status SUCCESS / FAILED / SKIPPED execution_message Details about the operation unresolved_issues_count Open issue count (release only) was_released Release status before action was_archived Archive status before action executed_at ISO 8601 timestamp
